decisions.title: Bug #7: key rollup segment state by physical segment (a month-boundary payer re-stamp orphans a billed gauge)
decisions.area: billing / rollup (src/rollup.rs, src/rollup/page.rs, src/rollup/close.rs, new src/rollup/rekey.rs)
decisions.context: Setup: auth mode shadow or enforce, with a ROLLUP=1 month closer. After a workspace change, or a feed-lag fallback stamp, the first month-crossing append emits month M's final under the old account A and then re-stamps to B. segment/A/... then keeps a frozen gauge. From the close of M+1 onward, CarryPage::segment bills A that gauge for every full month, even after the stream is deleted. B is billed correctly. The planned fix changes the key to segment/{project}/{stream_id}/{seg}, with the payer as an attribute. A one-shot migration at open folds the 5-part rows (greatest usage_version / accounted_through), drops carry cursors keyed by payer and keeps the identity check. The fix is roll-forward only: an older binary fails its carry closed on 4-part keys. Phantom rows that were already finalized are not reversed; no export exists yet, so nothing has been invoiced. Two further consequences from the plan: today the provisional usage fallback (src/product/usage.rs:100-118) also shows the previous payer phantom current-month storage; and under the fix, a legacy row whose account attribute disagrees with its key fails open() (the instance is not ready) instead of failing only close_month. The plan notes such a row is unreachable by construction, because apply_snapshot writes both together. Both bear on the rehearsal in option (b).
options: (a) Land the re-key and migration now as one commit. Delete rekey.rs once every ROLLUP=1 instance has opened under the new layout.
(b) Land it only after rehearsing the migration on a copy of a real rollup DB
(c) Defer (backward-compatible: status quo; storage keeps accruing to the previous payer after any transfer)
Sub-decision: reverse phantom month rows or artifacts already finalized, using explicit UsageCorrection records (an operator decision the plan leaves out of scope)
decisions.recommendation: (b), the program's lean. Held since 2026-09-21; do not land without Søren's explicit answer.
decisions.blocks: Correct storage billing in the release posture after any workspace transfer or fallback stamp; invoice export; the later rekey.rs deletion commit.

decisions.title: Named length limit for Producer-Id (a 65,503+ byte id panics the committer)
decisions.context: Found while planning item 53. A Producer-Id of 65,503 bytes or more makes the producer key longer than slatedb's u16::MAX key limit (33 + 65,503 > 65,535), and WriteBatch::put panics inside the committer. No header-length check exists. hyper's SSE_H1_MAX_BUF is only a soft threshold: reading hyper 1.10.1's source, not running it, a head of about 120 KB can parse at the default posture. The same gap on Stream-Seq was closed without a wire change (d148e1a4), but a producer key cannot drop its id.
options: Status quo (backward-compatible): no limit, and the committer panics on such an id

A length check in parse_producer answering the existing 400 invalid_producer, at a named limit (plan D4). The number is open: any value below the 65,503-byte panic threshold; routing keys use 1,024 bytes (b0a6ba65).
A new, separately named 400 code for an over-long Producer-Id
decisions.recommendation: Add the check with the existing 400 invalid_producer; the number is Søren's call.

decisions.title: Item 22 follow-up: retire the untyped-409 => ChangedIncarnation mapping on relayed reads
decisions.context: 74391f9c makes the owner answer a typed {refused: verdict} body on the internal page route, so cursor_beyond_tail now crosses the fleet intact. An untyped 409 without Streams-Replay-To is still read as ChangedIncarnation, which covers older owners during a rolling deploy and the receiver's 409 stale_target. Retiring that mapping alone would turn a genuine recreate's stale_target into a retryable 503 temporarily_unavailable at the product edge. An SDK would then retry a dead cursor until the coordinator's registry cache turns over. Typing stale_target in the same commit is blocked by the product.rs 4,205-line ceiling.
options: Keep the untyped-409 mapping (backward-compatible; what landed)
Retire it now and accept retryable 503s for genuine recreates until the cache turns over
Type stale_target on the owner first (after a verbatim move out of product.rs to make room), then retire the mapping
decisions.recommendation: Type stale_target first, then retire the mapping.
decisions.blocks: Removing the last status-derived verdict on the relayed read path (RUST-QUALITY.md forbids rebuilding domain decisions from HTTP status); the matching WIRE-MATRIX fleet-internal row.

decisions.title: Item 39: deploy supervise.ts turns every process death into a held, unauthenticated 500
decisions.area: deploy wrapper (deploy/app-server/supervise.ts and two byte-identical copies), RUNBOOK
decisions.context: When the child exits, the wrapper binds $PORT and serves 500 binary_exited with the stderr tail, forever and without authentication. A process death is therefore never restarted by the platform, contrary to RUNBOOK/OPERATIONS. Its hint ('check required env vars and that the binary is x86_64') is wrong for other causes. No detailed plan exists yet; the review's proposal is the reference.
options: Status quo (backward-compatible)

Review's change: exit(code or 1) if the child was ever TCP-ready and hold the diagnostic only when it never bound; bearer-gate stderrTail; an explicit hold-corpse env for bench/fleet/handoff-gate.sh; fix RUNBOOK.md:383-412 and :489-495; validate on a cloud service
decisions.recommendation: Land item 39 before item 38, which is the program's ordering. It still needs a plan and a cloud validation run.
decisions.blocks: Item 38; item 37 step B option 2 (exit on poison). Behind the wrapper, both would produce a 500 zombie instead of a restart.

decisions.title: Item 38: a dead critical loop stops the process (exit 1) instead of leaving a 503 zombie
decisions.context: Today a Critical loop that returns or panics leaves /health and /readyz answering 503 for the life of the process, while every other route keeps serving. The exit watchdog never sees it. ShardDirectory::shutdown also waits out its grace on an engine whose storage close failed, then drops the failure. The plan gives only the binary a process_root supervisor: its first critical exit requests the ordered stop (listener closed, loops joined, shards closed) and exits 1 naming the loop. Skeptic-promoted D4: with ROLLUP=1 and BILLING_MODE not required, a rollup DB open failure now exits the process instead of serving behind a 503. D5: a critical loop that ends before the rss-sampler registration makes run return with loops still running.
options: D1 status quo (backward-compatible): the 503 zombie stays until killed
D1 alternative: widen spawn_unready_watchdog to the supervisor's predicate and process::exit(1) after UNREADY_EXIT_AFTER_SECS (default 300 s, 0 disables), with no ordered stop
D1 alternative: process_root behind an env knob, off by default
D1 as planned: process_root escalation, ordered stop, exit 1. D2: land after item 39. D3: a held-interleaving test instead of a Loom model.
D4: approve the exit on a rollup-open failure explicitly, or keep serving behind 503
D5: accept the boot-window stranding as a recorded follow-up, or make ordered_stop also run on that error path
decisions.recommendation: Item 39 first, then item 38 as planned. D4 must be approved explicitly. D5 has no recorded recommendation.
decisions.blocks: Item 38's commits (planned, with skeptic corrections C1-C12 to apply first; not landed); a follow-up turning the unready watchdog's process::exit into an ordered stop.

decisions.title: Item 31: the queued-bytes charge belongs to the committer request, not the handler future
decisions.area: product append admission (src/quota.rs, src/product.rs append path)
decisions.context: A product append's queued_append_bytes charge is released when the handler future ends. A request that times out (10 s) or disconnects while the committer still holds it therefore stops counting, and the charge under-reports during stalls. Moving the charge to the queued request fixes that. But queued_bytes is one per-project counter, so a single wedged shard would pin the project's budget until its committer drains. Healthy shards and streams would then get 429 queued_bytes (no retry-after) or 429 project_memory_pressure. The exposure is bounded by queue capacity × request size.
options: Hold (backward-compatible: status quo)
Move the charge as planned
Move it and add a per-shard cap

Keep refusals keyed to handler-held bytes and report committer-held bytes of abandoned callers as a separate, non-refusing counter (for example abandoned_queued_bytes on /v1/debug/load). This is the plan's backward-compatible alternative, which it marks 'Not recommended': the latch and ceiling stay blind to committer-held memory, and it needs a second counter plus its own guard.

Sub-decisions raised by the skeptic: should 429 queued_bytes now carry retry-after (C5; the plan's §8 keeps it unchanged)? Does PROJECT_PRESSURE_MODEL_VERSION stay 1 (C4; the skeptic recommends keeping 1)?
decisions.recommendation: Hold, or pair the move with a per-shard cap.
decisions.blocks: An accurate project memory-pressure estimate during committer stalls.

decisions.title: Chain 45 -> 29: typed fork-read refusals (transient shard states become 503, one resolve mapping)
decisions.area: raw/product fork reads and fork creation (src/application/read.rs, src/http/read.rs)
decisions.context: The read adapter keeps a private ResolveError mapping that drifted: 500 shard_open_failed where every other surface answers shard_open. Fork reads and fork creation answer 500 internal for transient shard states (opening, moving, closing). A catalog read failure is reported as 'fork source x is gone'. The plan's §2.2 table rows are unlabelled (skeptic C3). The memo calls these the '503s (D2, D5)'.
options: Keep today's 500s and the private mapping (backward-compatible)

Approve as planned (every row of the plan's §2.2 table): raw fork GET/HEAD and raw fork PUT on an opening/moving/closing own, source or ancestor shard -> 503 shard_opening/shard_moving/shard_closing + Retry-After (was 500 internal); product fork read, same condition -> 503 temporarily_unavailable (retryable; still no Retry-After); a raw fork GET, or a raw fork PUT, whose own, source or ancestor shard failed to open -> 500 shard_open (was 500 internal); on raw GET/HEAD, internal segment-read and raw SSE connect refusals, the open-failure code shard_open_failed -> shard_open with message 'open shard <prefix>: <error>', and the shard-opening message 'shard is opening; retry' -> 'shard not currently serving here; retry' (same status, code and header); an ancestor served elsewhere stays 500 internal, now with no Streams-Replay-To and a message naming the shard and owner; the catalog-failure message 'fork source x is gone' -> 'fork source x could not be read: <error>'; fork reads and creation adopt as External custody (not wire-visible)

Scope sub-decision: fix the product read's missing Retry-After (needs a product.rs move) and ConsumerFailure dropping retry_after_secs (consumer.rs, no ceiling) in-chain, or record both as follow-ups (skeptic C8)
decisions.recommendation: Approve the 503s and the code rename.
decisions.blocks: Chain 45 -> 29 (four commits planned with skeptic corrections C1-C11; none landed).

decisions.title: Fork read whose own shard is owned elsewhere: 409 + Streams-Replay-To, relay, or 500
decisions.context: The plan answers a fork read whose OWN shard is foreign with 409 not_ring_owner + Streams-Replay-To (today: 500 internal). Skeptic C2 found that non-fork reads do not answer 409 by default: they relay through remote_read_page whenever allow_remote is set and the read is not a long-poll (the raw default; product always). So 409 would make fork reads the only reads that redirect. No peer relay exists for stitched reads. The memo calls this D3.
options: Keep 500 internal (backward-compatible; the router never converges on forks)
409 not_ring_owner + Streams-Replay-To, as planned
Relay like non-fork reads (needs a stitched-read peer relay; see FORK-CROSS-OWNER)
decisions.recommendation: Undecided: the memo asks Søren to weigh the planned 409 against relaying like non-fork reads.

decisions.title: Cross-owner fork stitching and creation are unsupported in multi-instance rings
decisions.context: A fork routes by its own name (RouteHash::for_stream), so in a multi-instance ring its source or ancestors usually live on another instance. Reading or creating such a fork answers 500 today and will still answer 500 after chain 45 -> 29, only honestly and without a redirect. SSE fork sources also type-erase stitched failures into anyhow.
options: Accept and document as a limitation (backward-compatible: status quo)
Build a peer relay of ancestor spans for stitched reads and fork creation
decisions.recommendation: None recorded. The plan flags it as a real product gap in multi-instance rings.
decisions.blocks: Fork use on multi-instance cells; the relay option of CHAIN-45-29-FOREIGN-OWN.

decisions.title: Registry/catalog read faults: 500 vs retryable 503 on public preludes and the remaining internal receivers
decisions.area: product public surface, fleet-internal receivers (product.rs preludes, product/scan.rs, http.rs internal segment routes)
decisions.context: Item 30 (5c0e62d6) made three fleet-internal receivers answer 503 temporarily_unavailable for a registry fault instead of 404. The http.rs internal segment-read and segment-close twins still use err_resp without retryable. internal_segment_close alone gates on desc_alive, so it answers 404 for a dead descriptor even when the epoch matches.

Answer 503 temporarily_unavailable (retryable) on the public preludes and fork catalog faults; this adds a Registry variant to ForkReadError
Unify the http.rs internal twins on internal_desc once http.rs has line budget (adds retryable to two internal error bodies)
Decide once whether internal_segment_close should gate on liveness

decisions.title: Unboundable committer whole-body mutants block the queue-refusal chain and item 80's v2-field deletion
decisions.area: quality gate / shard committer (src/shard/transaction/mod.rs, finalize.rs, shard.rs committer_loop)

A preparatory commit that bounds every wait in the shard:: tests, so a blank-body mutant fails fast
Narrow the chain (skeptic C2/C3): drop the stage site from C2, prove run and write locally under CI's timeout and defer whatever times out, and make C3's local mutation run a hard gate before C4

decisions.title: Chain 46/47/48 -> 23: a retiring engine, a closed store or a stopped committer answers retryable 503 (D1-D5, D7)
decisions.area: raw/product append and consumer queue ops (src/queue.rs QueueRefusal, src/application/consumer.rs)
decisions.context: Queue ops reply Result<_, String> and callers match on string prefixes. An engine retired before enqueue answers 429 'append queue full'. A write fenced by ErrorKind::Closed is 500 internal. A committer that stops abnormally leaves queued appends waiting for a 408 after up to 10 s, and queued queue ops get 500 'committer dropped request'. The plan types these as QueueRefusal (plus an AppendErr storage disposition) and maps them in one table.
options: Keep today's answers (backward-compatible): D1 keep 429, D2 keep 500, D4 keep 500 internal, D5 keep 500 internal. D3 has no meaningful alternative: today's answer is a lost reply.
D1: engine retired before enqueue -> raw 503 shard_moving + Retry-After: 1, product 503 temporarily_unavailable, raw PUT with body 503 shard_moving (was 429 overloaded / rate_limited)
D2: a group write, handle load or billing-row read failing with ErrorKind::Closed -> 503 shard_moving / temporarily_unavailable + Retry-After: 1 (was 500 internal / append_failed)
D3: an op still queued when the committer stops abnormally -> immediate 503 shard_moving (the op already taken keeps 408)
D4: consumer pull/settle/PUT/GET/DELETE on a retired engine -> 503 shard_moving (retryable; the SDK auto-retries) instead of 500 internal
D5: an unreadable generation fence -> 503 queue_unavailable (was 500)
D7 (informational): the 404 consumer_not_found / 409 consumer_deleted messages become fixed text instead of committer strings

decisions.title: Chain 46/47/48 -> 23 D6: a new 409 consumer_lifecycle_conflict code for a lost DELETE CAS
decisions.context: A consumer DELETE whose lifecycle CAS loses a race (GenerationConflict, LifecycleConflict) answers 500 internal today. So does one whose record vanished before the CAS, which in practice is unreachable because tombstones persist. The plan introduces a new public code, retryable: a re-issued DELETE re-reads and answers 204.

409 consumer_lifecycle_conflict (retryable: true) for a lost CAS, and 404 consumer_not_found for a vanished record

decisions.title: Item 51: a rate-limited raw close-with-final leaves the stream sealing
decisions.context: A raw close-with-body installs its durable Sealing intent BEFORE the per-stream limiter admits it. A 429 limit_*_per_sec close then leaves the stream stranded: raw appends get 409 stream_closed + Stream-Closed: true, product appends 409 sealed, and other closes or seals are refused, until the exact retry. The fix hoists admit_usage above install_intent, a line-neutral one-statement move. RELEASE-PRODUCT-SURFACE round 7 documents intent retention across transient refusals as deliberate, so this narrows a documented behaviour. Skeptic C1: an owed-final exact retry still renews its lease before admission.
options: D1 docs only (backward-compatible): keep the order and document that a throttled close strands the stream until its exact retry or another seal
D1 as planned: the limiter decides before the seal intent, so a 429'd close leaves the stream open
D2: when a close hits both the limiter and a refusing intent CAS, it answers 429 before 409 sealed. Alternative: a read-only desc.sealing pre-check so 409 wins (not recommended; racy).
D3: a close the CAS refuses has already spent its limiter tokens (matches every other post-admission refusal). Alternative: refund, which needs a new UsageService API.
D4: correct RELEASE-PRODUCT-SURFACE.md:651-658 in place with a dated note, or add an erratum section
D5: leave the other post-intent pre-enqueue refusals and the product seal-with-final twin for a follow-up item
decisions.recommendation: Approve D1, with D2-D5 as the plan recommends.
decisions.blocks: Item 51's single commit (planned, not landed); SEL-001's full-coverage claim in the scenario map.

decisions.title: Item 50: tracker eviction orphans a fully absorbed stream's pressure binding
decisions.context: The tracker sweep evicts a zero-debt entry whose streams are still resident, orphaning their StreamPressureBinding. This matters only with a saturated tracker. The direct fix is never to evict an entry anything else holds. But a resident stream's binding holds its project for about 905 s after the last append (absorber age 300 s + handle idle 600 s + tick), so sustained first-seen churn above about 18 projects/s would get 503 project_tracker_capacity (today about 54/s). HANDLE_IDLE_EVICT_SECS=0 would let the tracker fill permanently.
options: Status quo (backward-compatible): keep today's eviction and occupancy
(a) The fix, plus MAX_TRACKED_PROJECTS 16,384 -> 32,768 (about 16 MiB worst case) and refusing HANDLE_IDLE_EVICT_SECS=0 at boot
(b) The fix at today's cap, accepting the lower churn ceiling
(c) Re-point the handle's binding to the live entry: a synchronization change in shard.rs and publish.rs that selects Loom and leaves the admit-window race open
decisions.blocks: Item 50 (planned; skeptic C1/C2 corrections reshaped the cap decision).

decisions.title: Item 37 step B: readiness when a process-wide lock is poisoned
decisions.context: Several process-wide owners deliberately panic on poison: peer URLs, the ownership view, admission streams, the usage map and the billing cursors. A poisoned one makes every request that touches it panic and reset, while /health stays 200. Step A (a0185c3b) makes each such reset visible as tasks.connection_panics on /v1/debug/load, plus an ERROR log line. The router's own comment says mid-life failures deliberately do not unready an instance.
options: (3) No readiness change (backward-compatible). Add tasks.poisoned: [owner] to /v1/debug/load and alert on connection_panics growth.
(1) Owners expose is_poisoned() and /health answers 503 naming the owner. Risk: a poison pill sent to every instance takes the fleet out of rotation.
(2) A poisoned owner requests shutdown so the platform restarts it. Same fleet risk, but self-healing; depends on item 39.
decisions.recommendation: (3) now; decide (1) or (2) with WP-15's readiness slice.

decisions.title: Item 88 step 2: a strict offset decoder refuses non-canonical tokens
decisions.area: raw reads, SSE, internal segment-read, fork offsets (src/offsets.rs)
decisions.context: Four kinds of non-canonical offset token are silently decoded as a position today: a first digit above '7', a multibyte char, nonzero pad bits, and nonzero in_block bits. Reads then start, and forks are created, at a position the client never held. 2ced74c7 pins this lax reading so step 1 (33d8d3dd, one codec) could not move it. Refusing these tokens is 400 invalid_offset, or 400 invalid_fork_offset, which needs new Display text. Crockford aliases (O->0, I/L->1) and lowercase are also accepted today; our encoder never emits them.
options: Keep the lax reading (backward-compatible)
Refuse only the four structural classes and keep accepting Crockford aliases and lowercase
Strict-all: accept only the 32 uppercase canonical characters
A log-only window first (needs a new /metrics counter, itself an edge change; not recommended)
decisions.recommendation: Refuse only the four structural classes: no server ever minted one.

decisions.title: Offset epoch ceiling: segment ids at or above 2^30 collide in the offset encoding
decisions.context: The offset encoder drops epoch bits 30-31, so segment 2^30+k's tokens collide with segment k's. The step-1 codec documents the ceiling and its properties cover epochs below 2^30. Reaching it takes about 2^30 segment allocations on one stream.
options: Keep it documented only (backward-compatible; what step 1 did)
Cap segment-id allocation at 2^30 in segmap (IdExhausted); no wire change
Make encode fallible (touches all five render paths)
decisions.recommendation: Cap allocation at 2^30 in segmap.
decisions.blocks: Nothing immediate; it closes a latent silent collision.

decisions.title: hyper h1 request-head / idle keep-alive deadline default = 120 s (landed in 71345c03)
decisions.context: serve_h1 installed no hyper timer, so the documented 30 s head deadline was silently off, and headless or idle sockets were held forever. 71345c03 installs it, and it doubles as the idle keep-alive bound, at 120 s instead of hyper's 30 s. The platform edge's upstream pool idle is undocumented, and closing idle connections sooner than a client pool reuses them turns stale reuse into origin-less failures. 120 s is above every client pool idle in the repo; the bench pools moved from 120 s to 60 s. bench/sse-probes/ka-slope.sh parks sockets for 40 s.
options: Keep 120 s until measured (what landed)
hyper's 30 s default: a better fd bound, with a risk of edge 502s on stale upstream reuse
Lower it via SSE_H1_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS once a staging soak has measured the edge's upstream pool idle (ka-slope.sh needs at least 40 s)
decisions.recommendation: Keep 120 s and measure the edge's pool idle in the staging soak (follow-up F-E); lower it through the knob if the edge idles sooner.
decisions.blocks: The field posture number for release.

decisions.title: Stream-TTL / expiry.idle ceiling = 2^32-1 s (about 136 years), landed in efe12b2e
decisions.area: raw Stream-TTL and product expiry.idle (src/application/creation/ttl.rs MAX_TTL_SECS)
decisions.context: Unbounded TTLs wrapped expires_at_ms into the past: a 201 for a dead-on-arrival stream, a handler panic under overflow checks, and legacy windows that made forks unforkable. efe12b2e refuses values above 4,294,967,295 through the existing 400 invalid_ttl / invalid_config arms. Persisted windows saturate to 'never'. Omitting the TTL is the canonical 'never expires'. Conformance 332/0/6 was re-run on the release binary. This is a wire-contract number.
options: Keep 2^32-1 s (what landed; it admits the common 'forever' sentinels 2147483647 and 4294967295)
A human-round ceiling of 100*365*86,400 = 3,153,600,000 s (one const, three test literals, two doc rows)
Clamp instead of refusing (rejected: MAX+1 and MAX+2 would compare as the same configuration)
decisions.recommendation: Keep 2^32-1 s unless Søren prefers the round number.
decisions.blocks: Nothing; the value can still change cheaply.

decisions.title: Raw Stream-TTL: 0 stays admitted (a 201 for a stream dead in the same millisecond)
decisions.context: Stream-TTL: 0 gives expires_at_ms = created_ms, so desc_alive is false in the same millisecond: the same '201 then dead' symptom, reached without overflow. The product surface already refuses 0 (spec §13: 'positive'). The conformance suite never sends 0. efe12b2e kept it admitted and pinned that explicitly. The '0' test row is also the only killer of a `>` -> `>=` mutant at http.rs.
options: Keep 0 admitted on raw (backward-compatible; what landed)
Refuse 0 on both surfaces: admit_ttl accepts 1..=MAX_TTL_SECS and the wire matrix row becomes 1..=4294967295
decisions.recommendation: Keep admitted, as landed.

decisions.title: Follow-up F-D: raw Stream-Expires-At accepts a past instant (201 for a dead-on-arrival stream)
decisions.context: The raw Stream-Expires-At has no future check, while product expiry.at refuses a past instant. So a past instant answers 201 for a stream that is already expired. create_stream is unwrap_used-ratcheted, so the fix needs a reason re-decision or a helper outside it.
options: Keep accepting (backward-compatible)
Refuse a past instant on the raw surface with 400 invalid_request, matching product
decisions.recommendation: Refuse on raw (recorded as follow-up F-D; a wire change needing approval).

decisions.title: A settle extend's visibilityMs: 0 is floored to 1 s (landed in 2374751d)
decisions.context: 2374751d bounds a settle's retry delayMs to 0..12 h and an extend's visibilityMs to 1 s..12 h, the window a pull already keeps. Before, 9e18 wrote a lease that never expired, and u64::MAX wrapped or panicked the committer. The one change beyond bounding absurd values: extends[].visibilityMs: 0 used to mean 'visible now' and is now 1 s. 'Visible now' is spelled retries[{delayMs: 0}]. Nothing in the repo or the SDK relied on extend-0. Lease rows an older binary already wrote unbounded are not healed; an ack or a consumer delete clears them.
options: Keep the 1 s floor (what landed)
Restore extend-0 = 'visible now' by routing extends through bounded_window_ms(.., 0) as a fourth entry point (backward-compatible)
decisions.recommendation: Keep the floor.

decisions.title: An unparseable knob value or an unknown BILLING_MODE/ROLLUP word refuses boot (item 41 C3 D1 + item 32 D-32a)
decisions.context: 54 numeric knobs silently take their default when the value does not parse. Skeptic C5: 52 in production, because COMPACTOR_POLL_MS and COMPACTOR_MAX_CONCURRENT already refuse through clap. Any BILLING_MODE other than 'required' silently means off, and any ROLLUP other than '1' means 'not the rollup owner'. So BILLING_MODE=Required runs a production cell with volatile billing fallbacks. After the change, validate() exits 1 with 'configuration invalid (N problem(s))' before any store opens. No in-repo deploy source carries a bad value, but env set on live Compute apps is not visible from the repo. Non-UTF-8 values would still silently default (C10). The src/sse/budget.rs doc contract (warn and default) changes with it.
options: Status quo (backward-compatible): silent default
Ship a ConfigNotice warning for one release (boot continues on today's meaning), then flip to refusal once the logs show zero hits
Refuse at validate() now (41 C3 and 32 C4 as planned, plus a regression test that deploy/profiles/compute-1g.env parses)

decisions.title: Item 40: the fleet heartbeat gets its own supervised cadence (what does a fresh heartbeat prove?)
decisions.context: The heartbeat PUT is step 1 of one serial fleet tick, behind about 9 store ops. In a store brownout every instance drops every peer, and they fence each other. decisions.title: Item 54: canonical_arg saturates large whole floats and diverges from the SDK beyond 2^53 (watch value encoding)
decisions.context: Review item 54 (impact low, effort S) was not started. canonical_arg renders a whole float that is neither i64 nor u64 as `f as i64`, which saturates at i64::MAX (the review's red uses 1e19 vs 2e19, which today encode the same). The SDK prints String(v), so the server and SDK encodings differ for numbers beyond 2^53, and large exact integer ids also differ because JavaScript cannot hold them. The review's change: canonical_arg returns Option and renders the float branch only within +/-(2^53-1); the SDK throws for unsafe integers and accepts bigint; a shared value-encoding vector (a Rust test plus sdk/scripts/watch-value-vector.mjs) pins both. This changes watch value encoding on the server and in the SDK, so it needs wire approval.
options: Leave as is (backward-compatible; large values keep diverging between server and SDK)
Land the review's change on both server and SDK, with the shared vector
decisions.recommendation: None recorded; the item was not planned.

decisions.title: Item 56: product DELETE answers in the raw-surface error shape; the CreationFailure status table is duplicated
decisions.area: product DELETE error rendering (src/product.rs, src/http.rs product_delete / creation_error_response)
decisions.context: Review item 56 (impact low, effort S) was not started. Product DELETE dispatches to the pass-through http::product_delete and renders errors via err_resp, so they carry no retryable field and no cache-control; WIRE-MATRIX.md records this as a known leak. The 10-arm CreationFailure status table exists byte-identical in src/http.rs and src/product.rs. The review's change adds http::creation_failure_status beside creation_error_response, hoists product's Creation arm into creation_failure_response (forwarding retry_after), has the DELETE arm call creation_service().delete directly and deletes product_delete. The review describes the WIRE-MATRIX update as 'a deliberate additive wire change' (first red: a DELETE of a never-created stream must carry error.retryable == false and cache-control: no-store).
options: Leave as is (backward-compatible; the documented leak stays)
Land the review's change, an additive wire change to product DELETE error bodies and headers
decisions.recommendation: None recorded; the item was not planned.

decisions.title: Proposed item: internal_sweep_segment buffers its body before authentication (same defect as item 52)
decisions.context: Verified at HEAD: internal_sweep_segment (src/product.rs, about lines 3332-3344) takes `body: Bytes`, so axum buffers the request body before fleet_operation_authorized runs. Unauthenticated callers can therefore make the server buffer up to 2 MiB, the defect item 52 (2f2c3015) fixed for the telemetry-append receiver. The item 52 plan (§1.5, §8.1) records it as the only other handler using a buffering body extractor and recommends it as its own item. The fix is the same pattern plus a verbatim move, because product.rs is at its 4,205-line ceiling. The reviewer excluded it from item 52.
options: Leave as is
Its own item: move the handler out of product.rs verbatim, then authenticate before reading the body (as 2f2c3015 did)
decisions.recommendation: Its own item (plans10 §8.1).

decisions.title: Proposed item: `_usage` drain step 1 has no byte budget
decisions.context: Recorded in the item 52 plan (§1.3, §8.3). billing::drain_once step 1 takes up to 64 spooled read batches of about 1 MiB (estimated) each with no byte budget; DRAIN_MAX_BYTES applies only from step 2 on. Such a body can exceed even MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES (32 MiB default) on the local path and wedge `_usage` with 413 too_large, the sender requeueing the same batch every round. Not measured; item 52 closed only the relay-side 2 MiB mismatch.
options: Leave as is until measured
Measure a spooled backlog, then add a byte budget to step 1 as its own item
decisions.recommendation: Needs measurement and its own item (plans10 §8.3).

decisions.title: Unreproduced 500 on one append right after a split in the capacity leg
decisions.context: Batch 12's local gate reported GATEFAIL-capacity: in post_split_throughput_scales one append was answered 500 at about 8.6 s, right after the split. No production code had changed since the previous green gate. Batch 12 (a7f3167d + 24c4c77a) was pushed once three isolated re-runs of the capacity leg passed; CI for 24c4c77a was green on all three workflows. The reproduction attempts came after the push: 60 isolated runs, 40 runs under 8 busy cores and further runs under 16 busy cores never produced a 500. Under load the only failure was a different, benign one: the single-shot split declines when the parent's seal misses its deadline (2 of 40 runs; the scaler resumes the pending intent later). The suspects are review item 47 (a write racing a closing store reported as 500 internal instead of 503 shard_moving, part of the held queue chain) and ResolveError::OpenFailed on a child-shard open, which also maps to 500.
options: Wait; if it recurs, add the 10-line instrumentation in topology_scaling.rs KeyedAppender::post to print the 500's body (program stance)
Land the instrumentation now
Prioritise the queue chain (item 47) as the likely fix
decisions.recommendation: Instrument only if it recurs.

decisions.title: Confirm or revert the edge-visible changes landed without prior sign-off
decisions.context: The memo's list 'Changes I made at the edge' holds nine behaviour changes. Items 1-5 make a race window or corrupt-storage case answer what the documented race-free path already answers (no new codes). Items 6-9 touch operator or fleet-internal surfaces only; the memo's own sentence says '6-8' but lists nine items, and '6-9' is the right reading. Items 1 (the raw-PUT half of item 9) and 5 (item 64) have no correct backward-compatible alternative per their plans; the others had one that was not taken. For item 86 the author chose 'wait 100 ms, then hand to the live loop' over the review's 're-read without reaching the live loop', so a session the ring can serve is not stalled behind a durable hole. H1-IDLE-DEADLINE, TTL-CEILING, STREAM-TTL-ZERO and VISIBILITY-FLOOR are listed separately.
options: Confirm all (status quo after landing)
Item 44: revert to a route-only layer with no fallback (anonymous 404/405 again, byte-identical wire)
Item 52: keep the relay at 2 MiB after authentication
Item 86: drop the FEED_NO_PROGRESS add in catch_up::stalled so no_progress stays drive-only
Item 33: revert to parking until the next append or the lease nap (backward-compatible); honouring the peer's Retry-After would be a further, separate change
Item 34: the 'honoured move-ins only' eager-open form
Item 9 D2: keep product 409 gone for a live forked winner
Item 55: read a corrupt lane row as missing (not recommended: silent loss of idempotence)
decisions.recommendation: Confirm all nine; the program recommends none of the reverts.
decisions.blocks: Nothing already landed; a revert is one small commit each.

edge_changes_made: b0a6ba65 (bug #2): an append Prisma-Routing-Key header, or a seal routingKey, containing bytes outside the header-text class (visible ASCII, space, tab), such as seal routingKey 'café' or a non-text Prisma-Routing-Key header, is now 400 invalid_routing_key on both writers. Before, it was 200, with the record and idempotency hash filed under the default key ''. The 1,024-byte limit is unchanged; over-long keys were already 400.

6faf4757 (bug #3): a product watch wait that reaches a non-owner is refused through the shared resolve mapping (409 + Streams-Replay-To; 503 + Retry-After while the shard opens) before it parks. Before, it answered 200 invalidated:false forever. A cold non-owner refuses without opening the owner's shard.

1994fc25 (bug #4): a consumer pull returns by its deadline even when the dead-letter handoff is blocked (it used to spin forever, even at waitMs=0). It always delivers leases the same Receive granted to other keys; before, those were dropped and burned an attempt.
d2e87129 + 3dfb970f (bug #1): keyed catch-up reads no longer silently skip durable records after a postings-cache over-claim or stale publish.
84f80b75 (bug #5): the billing tombstone walk covers every project in the cell. Clean terminal rows of non-deployment projects no longer bill storage at every month close.

c19cc2f0 (bug #8): the absorber never waits for pool bytes while it holds some. Two gathers that both needed to grow could each hold part of the shared pool and wait forever, parking every absorber in the process with no log (needs two or more shard absorbers and ABSORB_GLOBAL_GATHERS >= 2; the certified compute-1g profile sets 1). A grow the pool refuses now defers the chunk. No wire change.
5292e3e3 (bug #6): the feed's retry task no longer reads and publishes records, so a solo subscriber is no longer lag-cut by its own records.

668bc80c + 5d60dc63 (bug #9): an append routed by a descriptor that predates a split or merge is retried on the successor (up to 4 attempts, waits 10/20/30 ms) instead of answering 409 sealed for a live collection. An unreadable refresh is a retryable segment_transition. A recreated name answers TargetIncarnationChanged instead of StreamClosed. Exhaustion carries Retry-After.

efe12b2e (rank 10): raw Stream-TTL above 4,294,967,295 s is 400 invalid_ttl, and product expiry.idle above it is 400 invalid_config. Before, only some values misbehaved: u64::MAX gave 201 for an already-expired stream; about 9.2e15 overflowed, giving a past expiry in release and a handler panic only under overflow checks (not the shipped release profile); other values above 2^32-1 were 201 with a far-future expiry and are now 400. Persisted windows saturate to 'never', so forks of legacy windows are creatable (was 409 fork_target_changed forever). Stream-TTL: 0 stays admitted on raw.
2374751d (rank 24): settle retries[].delayMs is clamped to 0..12 h and extends[].visibilityMs to 1 s..12 h. extend visibilityMs 0 now means 1 s, where it used to mean 'visible now'.

063a674d (registry cache): a registry read that raced a write no longer re-installs what it read, so readers on the process no longer see the pre-write descriptor, or a cached absence after a successful create on this process, for the 5 s TTL. A lost recreate invalidates instead of installing the winner it read (one extra GET). No wire change.

71345c03 (rank 17): every h1 connection gets a request-head/idle keep-alive deadline, default 120 s (new knob SSE_H1_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS, >0 only, shown in the config summary). Idle keep-alive and headless sockets now close at 120 s; in-flight responses and SSE are unaffected. Bench client pools went from 120 s to 60 s.
4247421f (rank 13): a raw SSE session sharing its default-lane feed now gets its standalone upToDate after a batch that carried nothing for it. Before, wire behaviour depended on subscriber count.

fd810688 (rank 15): a panicking shard opener or postings loader fails its load. The first caller gets a 500 with a different message, and later callers get the documented 503 shard_moving holdoff instead of 500 'shard open task vanished' forever.
ac9ab99e (rank 16): a catch-up through a sealed span whose engine reopened under the same owner is served. Before, it retried a closed cached engine every 100 ms forever.

d93b421b (rank 14): a live SSE tail whose engine retired under the same owner gets the typed nonterminal EOF (SourceCutoff::EngineRetired) instead of keep-alives forever. New /v1/debug/load key sse_livefeed.cutoff_engine_retired.
eb52b970 (rank 12): after a billing-sweep close, a customer's first request meets the 3 s base holdoff (503 shard_moving, Retry-After) instead of an escalated one of up to 60 s.

4bb51c0d (item 11): one unreadable routers/*.json no longer skips the fleet tick. Ring and peer publication, yield, eager open, return-home and the rebalancer run; only the scale decision is deferred. A slow router GET still delays the view by up to the 10 s population deadline. No wire change.
527d3d3a (rank 28): GET {collection}:scan now admits and debits the project read-byte quota. It gains 429 project_rate_limit + retry-after for a project in read debt.

f1c9e77e (rank 28 step B): POST .../consumers/{c}:pull admits the read-byte quota before taking any lease and debits the framed body. It gains 429 project_rate_limit, and the response now carries Cache-Control: no-store.

8dabca7f (rank 21, fleet-internal): the telemetry-append relay receiver on a non-owner answers 409 not_ring_owner + Streams-Replay-To (was 404). A missing key, non-canonical name or unparsable key is 400 missing_key / invalid_name / invalid_key.

06fb8d51 (item 49): an unreadable or non-UTF-8 _ops_metrics checkpoint fails the rollup step, which retries from the durable checkpoint, instead of re-merging every snapshot into the minute tier a second time. A 2xx system read page with no stream-next-offset is refused instead of being checkpointed as ''. No wire change.

5c0e62d6 (item 30, fleet-internal): the sweep-segment, queue-cursor and segment-scan receivers answer 503 temporarily_unavailable (retryable) for a registry read fault instead of 404 not_found, so a registry blip no longer disconnects every SSE subscriber of a sealed span.

74391f9c (item 22, fleet-internal): on the page route (streams-internal-read-page: 1) the owner answers a typed {refused: verdict} body. A cross-owner deliver=applied replay beyond the tail now surfaces as cursor_beyond_tail instead of target_mismatch; an untyped 409 still maps to ChangedIncarnation.

ee99975d (item 26): a graceful stop seals the active read window and drains it once, bounded by one TELEMETRY_DRAIN_SECS cadence. With a responsive store, reads metered before the stop are no longer dropped at SIGTERM. Caveats from the plan: deltas metered by connections aborted in the same instant can still land after the seal, and when the sealed queue is full (a long ledger outage) the active window remains the hard-loss window. No wire change.

a8c99c23 (item 25): a content append with more records than a fresh bucket can hold is 413 payload_too_large (raw) / body_too_large (product), with no retry-after, before TTL renewal and before any seal intent. Before, it was 429 limit_records_per_sec (raw) / 429 rate_limited (product) with retry-after: 1, forever. Bytes above a fresh bucket were already 413 (admit_usage's arm, now deleted); they are now refused at the same early point. Boot refuses limit postures that cannot admit one unit (LIMIT_BURST_SECS=0, NaN, negative, infinite capacity, sub-token request bucket). The /v1/debug/load limiter counters now count transient 429s only.

12ad5134 (item 57): a fleet outbox whose _ops_events append or encode fails returns that error, so the telemetry loop's 'fleet event drain' warning fires; it used to return Ok(0) with no log while pending events grew. The next tick retries the same ids. No wire change.

f499d590 + bbd23d13 (item 9): a raw PUT in the stale-snapshot window over an expired source with live forks answers 409 gone (was 201 + fresh epoch, which stranded every fork). A raw PUT whose CAS declines a soft-deleted winner answers 409 gone (was 200 'exists').
e7c7ad87 (item 9): a product create that loses the recreate CAS to a live forked incarnation gets the idempotent comparison (200 / 409 config_mismatch / 403 wrong_key) instead of 409 gone.

517f4fa1 (item 55): an append whose producer or Stream-Seq lane row does not decode is refused 500 internal (raw) / 500 append_failed (product), with nothing written. Before, it was accepted with the idempotence fence silently dropped. Legacy 16- and 24-byte producer rows stay readable.

7c4f8606 (item 33): a live SSE read that failed or made no progress is re-driven on a per-session backoff (250 ms doubling to 5 s) instead of waiting for the next append or the lease nap. A sealed-span peer answering 429/503 is re-read on that backoff, and its Retry-After is not consulted. Timing only.
8f590ec5 (item 53): SSE_H1_MAX_BUF below 8,192 is a boot-time configuration error (exit 1, named among the problems). Before, it panicked after bootstrap's side effects.

d148e1a4 (item 53): a Stream-Seq longer than 65,535 bytes is no longer copied into the tail row, so it can no longer wedge the stream (stored_tail used to refuse every later load). Rows that fit are byte-identical; no wire change.

85017d84 + 729c52ac (item 64, latent state only): a split or merge the segment map refuses stays pending. Writers to the parents' range then get the bounded wait and a retryable 503 segment_transition instead of a false final closure. The split/merge counters and *_committed ops events stop counting a publication that never happened.

2fb92fb9 (item 86): an empty SSE catch-up page waits 100 ms before being read again (it spun at about 3M reads/s). /v1/debug/load sse_livefeed.no_progress now also counts empty catch-up pages, and catchup_retries counts a persistent hole at most once per 100 ms per session.

a1cf29f3 (item 67): /v1/debug/store shard_opens (and /operator/data.json) are counted per runtime directory, and ?swap=1 never resets them. Production values are unchanged (one directory per process).

6515a15d (item 34, fleet policy): the rebalancer moves only to active-ring members. The eager open admits exactly what the ring assigns to this instance, so the ring's owner of a shard overridden to a non-member opens it at its next tick. Before, a non-member target fenced the real owner about once a minute.

2f2c3015 (item 52, fleet-internal): the telemetry-append receiver authenticates before reading the body, so an unauthenticated upload is 401 before any body read (before, it was buffered first: 401 after buffering, or 413 once past 2 MiB). An authenticated relay may carry up to MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES (32 MiB default; 413 too_large above), instead of axum's implicit 2 MiB, so a receiver can briefly hold about 2x that per concurrent relay.
33fbd10e (item 44, operator surface): without the token, an unrouted /v1/debug path or a wrong method answers 401 instead of 404/405. With the token, or in Off mode, every answer is byte-identical.
a0185c3b (item 37 step A): a panicking request handler is logged at ERROR and counted. /v1/debug/load gains the additive key tasks.connection_panics (per runtime).

714abcc2 (F-G): a task that a closing runtime refuses is dropped after the supervisor's registration lock is released, removing a same-thread deadlock that hung runtime teardown (the CI hang) and could hang a production shutdown the same way.
6ef3bc64 (item 87): SSE source reads fail as a typed fatal-or-retryable error, and a retried read now logs its cause (retryable causes were dropped unlogged). No wire change.

aaf2baa5 (item 63 step A): the billing sweep's custody handshake uses SeqCst read-modify-writes, so a customer's external stamp and a sweep's custody install can no longer both miss each other; a debt-free sweep can no longer retire an engine a customer has adopted. No wire change.

4cb6263c (item 93): auth feed freshness is stamped by the refresher at the fetch it asked for, not by the source. A snapshot that bypasses the refresher reads as never fetched and fails closed, and a post-dated source stamp can no longer give a negative age. No wire change.

07db91a7 (item 41 C1): SCALE_COOLDOWN_SECS=inf means 'never re-scale'. It used to wrap to 'always re-scale' in release and panic in debug. A huge SCALE_HOT_EVALS no longer makes every hot multi-segment stream a merge candidate.

1791207a (item 65): a lease re-proves its project's placement on this cell. A subscription whose project is republished for another cell ends as a project_missing termination (403 at establishment) instead of continuing to deliver.

a73b7b79 (item 65): /v1/debug/auth calls a feed stale exactly when enforcement refuses it, using the instance window instead of the POLICY_STALENESS_MAX_SECS constant. This is identical in production, where the window is never changed.
fdc31b07 (item 32): --compactor-poll-ms given on argv now reaches the compactor (it was silently ignored). Environment-only deployments are unchanged.

46d4b7df (item 32): /health, /operator/billing.json and the drain read the clap BILLING_MODE/ROLLUP values. With --billing-mode required or --rollup 1 on argv, /health now holds 503 until the spool or rollup is ready (it was 200 and reported 'off'). The reverse mismatch no longer leaves /health at 503 forever. The boot summary loses the two env-copy keys.

e19c80c5 (item 35): one stream's corrupt row backs off that stream alone, with a named warn, while its lane-mates advance in the same flush. Before, the whole gather aborted and up to 1,024 streams backed off together. No wire change.
5d9d517f (item 27): an undecodable pending monthly artifact is logged at error level on every scan and stays in the outbox (it used to be skipped silently). /operator/billing.json is unchanged.
31fd9096 (item 27): a late byte-time correction that cannot fit i128 fails its rollup page instead of committing a month row the rollup can no longer read.
